text.p: Shares in Dassault Aviation and Dassault Electronique rallied on Wednesday on speculation about the implications for the two groups of the restructuring of the French defence and aerospace industries, dealers said.
Dassault Aviation shares were up 4.95 percent at 1,230 francs at 0930 GMT, while Dassault Electronique shares climbed 5.61 percent to 491.10 francs.
The bourse's CAC index was up 1.01 percent.

The government on Tuesday moved forward in its plan to merge Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale, describing the corporate structure of the groups and retaining the Privatisation Commission to decide on the parities.

"Aerospatiale's bankers have evaluated their firm at 25 billion francs and Dassault at just over 10 billion francs. Dassault's bankers put the two at around 12 billion francs. Apparently the government's advisers are closer to Aerospatiale's evaluation, but the Privatisation Commission will have the last word," a brokerage said in its daily stock comment.
"A bid will most likely be offered for the outstanding four percent float of Dassault Aviation," it said.

Dassault Electronique shares were up, another broker said, on related speculation it might take part in a joint Alcatel -Aerospatiale-Dassault bid for state-owned Thomson-CSF, the defence electronics group.
